I use stock tire pressures on the street, despite having thinner tires, on track I go by tire pressures after a 3 lap stint. After 3 laps I adjust tire pressures so all 4 are even, and tire temperatures are in their ideal range. Lower pressures create more heat, higher pressures lower heat, to a point, lower pressures give you more contact patch, to a point. If the pressure is too low the sidewall squirms too much and the contact patch deforms, if the pressure is too high you reduce the contact patch. Somewhere is the perfect compromise between sidewall stiffness, and contact patch, throw in alignment angles and then you have another way to tune the way the tires build temperature, and how you use the contact patch. It starts getting tricky when you consider that alignment angles change when you load or unload a suspension, or change the ride height, these changes are also affected by the compliance of the control arm bushings.
